Caye Caulker is a small coral island in the Caribbean Sea, about 15 km from Belize City. The exotic tropical jungle, intricately shaped caves opening into grottos, quality service and excellent cuisine make it an appealing place for a peaceful holiday.

Life moves at an unhurried pace here. Everything encourages you to slow down: a gentle breeze, swaying palm trees, crystal-clear water and a carefree atmosphere.

Alongside this relaxed way of spending your time, you can enjoy diving and a variety of water sports.

### Cayenne: a city with centuries of history

Cayenne is the administrative center and largest settlement of French Guiana. It takes its name from the nearby river of the same name. Founded in 1664, the city now has more than 50,000 inhabitants. Some of the country's most engaging sights can be found here.

The former splendor of this colonial capital, once part of a country known as a major pepper supplier to the world, can still be felt throughout the city. The streets are lined with colonial-style buildings with wrought-iron balconies draped in ornamental plants and flowers, while latticed shutters are decorated with tropical carnations. Beyond the historic colonial center, the architecture reminds you that you are already in the 21st century. Cayenne has many restaurants and cafés serving a wide variety of cuisines. Its markets are filled with produce to suit the diverse tastes of residents and visitors alike.

## Holidays in Cayenne

### Let's take a walk through Cayenne!

Cayenne is washed by the Atlantic Ocean. The city's main thoroughfare, Avenue du Général de Gaulle, is home to many leading sights: the Hôtel de Ville, built by Jesuits in 1890, the post office and the residence of the prefect of French Guiana. Two particularly beautiful places for a stroll are Place de Grenoble and Place des Palmistes. As you wander through them, you can admire architectural landmarks, pick up gifts for loved ones in souvenir shops, and visit the botanical garden or the Museum of French Guianese Culture. With its centuries of history, Cayenne has much to offer travelers.

The Cayo resort area is home to beautiful natural attractions: a baboon monkey sanctuary, a jaguar reserve, jungles, tropical forests, waterfalls, a zoo and caves with underground rivers.

In Cayo, visitors can go yachting, enjoy ecotourism, swim and sunbathe on the beaches. The remarkably clear seawater offers views of colorful tropical fish.

Cayo also attracts visitors because of its proximity to the barrier reef, just 30 km away, making it especially appealing to divers. A gentle breeze, swaying palms, crystal-clear water and a tranquil atmosphere all add to the appeal.

## Cali: a city of salsa, museums and colonial architecture

Cali is Colombia's third-largest city. Since sugar and coffee production began to develop here, the city has rapidly grown from a small prospectors' settlement into one of the country's major industrial and commercial centers.

Located in western Colombia and founded in the 16th century, Cali is the country's third most populous city. It has numerous historical and architectural landmarks. The 17th-century Iglesia de La Merced is the city's oldest religious building. Other attractions include Iglesia de San Antonio on a hill near central Cali and Plaza de Toros de Cañaveralejo, a bullring. Modern architecture is represented by the 185-meter Cali Tower, built in 1978 and described as the country's third-tallest skyscraper.

## Cali: a city for visitors

Many colonial-era buildings survive in Cali. The city also has numerous museums with rich collections covering different subjects and lush green parks. In the salsa dance halls, residents (caleños) and visitors dance the night away despite the humid climate. Tourism is an important part of the city, with plenty of restaurants, bars and fashionable shops.

## Camagüey: a beautiful corner of Cuba

This is the third-largest city on the island. Its most striking architectural feature is an unusual street layout whose origins date back to the era of the famous pirate Henry Morgan.

The city has countless squares, large and small, and winding narrow streets that form a veritable maze.

Buildings of considerable historical interest have also survived. Camagüey is known as the "city of tinajones" because of its residents' fondness for clay jars of all sizes. The city has many museums and a theater that hosts impressive performances by symphony and chamber orchestras.
